text:
Maya R: Heads up — saw a spike in token latency for tenant 'acme-corp' yesterday evening. Grafana shows token_p95 jumping ~3x for short responses (<=64 tokens). :eyes:
Sam P: hmm. Is that in the global token breakdown or route-scoped?
Maya R: Route-scoped (chat.generate), but our dashboard aggregates across orgs. The per-route panel has no workspace/tenant split — we only have host/kernel labels right now.
Leon G: That matches the kernel-selection A/B we ran. Small requests were routed to the quantized kernel fallback which increases per-token CPU by a bit, but batching behavior also changed. Could be KV cache churn for that tenant.
Tara S: Do we have any per-tenant KV cache hit-rate metrics? I thought we only export global kv_cache_hits/requests without org label.
Sam P: Right — current prometheus metrics look like:
```
kv_cache_hits_total 123456
kv_cache_requests_total 234567
```
No org label. We can add a label tenant_id but need to be careful about cardinality and PII.
Maya R: We should avoid raw org ids in metrics. Proposal: export tenant_hash label (sha256 truncated) and a workspace_tier label (free/prod/enterprise). That gives visibility without leaking PII.
Leon G: Agreed. Also want a token-level latency histogram with labels: kernel, route, tenant_hash, batch_size. Then we can slice p50/p95 per-tenant and see if batching heuristics are misfiring.
ops-bot: [deployment] metrics-exporter/feature/tenant-labels deployed to staging at 2026-03-17T22:10:02Z :white_check_mark:
Sam P: Nice. On staging I added a Grafana variable var-tenant and a templated query. Example PromQL for tenant p95:
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_latency_seconds_bucket{route="chat.generate",tenant_hash=~"$tenant"}[5m])) by (le))
```
Maya R: That helped isolate the tenant. On staging acme-hash shows p95 ~12ms vs global ~4ms.
Tara S: Do we also capture per-route kvcache eviction rate? If a tenant's prefix churn is high, their hit rate plummets and latency spikes.
Leon G: I pulled a flamegraph of runtime CPU during the spike window — attaching snippet:
```
flamegraph: runtime_main -> kernel_select -> run_quant_kv -> kv_lookup -> memcopy
samples: 980
```
Sam P: That suggests more memcopy/kv_lookup work per token for that tenant. Possibly their requests use many short prefixes preventing effective KV reuse.
Maya R: For mitigation we could: 1) increase tenant-specific KV partition size for heavy tenants, 2) prefer non-quant kernel for small seq lengths, 3) throttle rapid prefix writes. Which is lowest-risk?
Tara S: 3) throttle prefix writes is app-visible; risky. 1) and 2) are infra changes. I vote try (2) as canary — change routing policy to prefer full-precision kernel for seq<=64 for enterprise tenants.
Leon G: I'll prototype a routing rule: prefer_kernel=\"fp16\" when seq_len<=64 and tenant_tier=\"enterprise\". Need to add tenant_tier label to routing metadata (not metrics).
Sam P: Also add a per-tenant dashboard panel: token_latency_breakdown{tenant_hash=\"$tenant\"} with batch_size heatmap and kv_hit_rate. Will surface regressions quickly.
Maya R: One more: RBAC. Product wants tenants to see their own performance in UI. We must ensure prometheus/metrics only surface hashed tenant ids; RBAC mapping must live in backend (no org id in metrics).
Tara S: Noted. Security: let's store mapping in control plane and only allow authenticated requests to resolve a tenant_hash -> org. Audit log both lookups.
ops-bot: [jira] CREATED PERF-842: Add tenant_hash to kvcache metrics + per-route token histogram. Assigned to @Sam P, target: 2026-03-24.
Sam P: I'll run the change on staging today, capture 48h of metrics, and post a short fallout doc.
Maya R: Thanks — once staging looks good we can roll a canary to prod for one region and one enterprise tenant. :thumbsup:
Leon G: I'll also add a small perf test that simulates many short-prefix requests to reproduce the hit.
Tara S: Slack reminder: let's discuss in perf sync tomorrow 09:00 PT. Agenda: metrics labels, routing rule, RBAC mapping, and rollout plan.
Maya R: cheers everyone.
